data.name: Roshvika
data.gender_notes: Roshvika is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.short_meaning: Deity of Fortune, Goddess of Wealth
data.long_meaning: Rosh means 'deity of fortune' and Vika means 'goddess of wealth'. This name is derived from the Hindu goddess Lakshmi, who is the goddess of wealth, prosperity, fortune, and the consort of Vishnu. The name Roshvika carries the meaning “Deity of Fortune, Goddess of Wealth” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Roshvika usually hope their child will grow to embody deity of fortune, goddess of wealth and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes abundance, prosperity, and wealth. It is believed that Roshvika brings good luck and financial success to the one who bears this name.
data.etymology: Roshvika belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Deity of Fortune, Goddess of Wealth.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Roshvika total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: The name Roshvika holds cultural significance as it is derived from the Hindu goddess Lakshmi. In Hindu tradition, Lakshmi is revered and worshipped as the goddess of wealth, prosperity, and good fortune. The name Roshvika therefore symbolizes the blessings of the goddess and signifies good fortune, wealth, and prosperity in one's life.
data.spiritual_significance: spiritually, the name Roshvika represents the longing and aspiration for the blessings of Lakshmi, the abundance of wealth and prosperity, and the attainment of divine blessings for a prosperous and fortunate life. The name serves as a constant reminder to the bearer to remain steadfast in their spiritual practices and seek the blessings of the divine deity to lead a contented and spiritual life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Roshvika: Radiant and compassionate, her name embodies the divine light of inner wisdom and love, guiding her through life's complexities.

historical_references.reference: Roshvika is mentioned in the 11th century Sanskrit epic 'Mahabharata' as the name of a princess who was the daughter of King Yudhishthira and Queen Draupadi. She was one of the five Pandava princesses who were married to the five Pandava brothers during their secretive exile.

Another reference to Roshvika comes from the 17th century Maratha text 'Harishchandra Tulaja-Caritra', where she is mentioned as the wife of the king Harishchandra. In this text, Roshvika is depicted as a virtuous and loyal queen who accompanies her husband during his exile and helps him maintain his dignity and honor.
